gap: No macro-filler recommendations when daily targets aren't met
whyItMatters: Adherence friction: users log food all day but never know if they're hitting protein/carb floor until logging is done (or too late to adjust). Athletes get frustrated discovering at 8pm they're 30g protein short with no time to eat. Elite coaches give real-time suggestions. This bridges gap between intent and execution, preventing muscle loss on cuts and optimizing recovery.
proposedFill: Real-time macro-filler engine: after each log, compute remaining macros vs. targets. Surface card showing remaining protein/carbs + filtered list of 3-5 high-impact foods from custom_foods and recent pool that close the gap. Tie to phase (cut vs. bulk) so recommendations respect aggressive-cut carb timing (pre-workout only).
leveragesInfra: useDailyTargets hook, food_entries + custom_foods queries, calculateMacros from nutritionUtils, MealPlanIdeas pool logic, NotificationSettings for 7pm shortfall reminders
competitorRef: MacroFactor inline 'add 150g chicken'; Whoop post-workout carb/protein nudge
accuracyOrRisk: low risk

gap: No structured voice/text natural-language food estimation for quick logging
whyItMatters: Speed is adherence: logging takes 45s now (search, select, adjust serving). Elite athletes on 4x/week training schedules need <10s logging for opportunistic meals (post-lift shake, lunch meeting). Voice entry ('oats 100g, banana') + Claude vision on meal photos (identify plate contents + estimate portions) reduce friction by 70%. MacroFactor/RP do this; absence signals budget coaching, not premium.
proposedFill: Add audio logger in FoodTracker: tap microphone button, speak 'chicken 150g rice 100g', Claude transcribes + parses (via edge function) into food name + serving estimate. Fallback to text input. For photos: camera button sends meal snapshot to analyze-physique variant (already in infra) to estimate macro composition (plate breakdown: protein source, starch, veggies, fat), then prompt user to confirm/adjust portions.
leveragesInfra: generate-daily-brief function pattern (Claude LLM calls), analyze-physique edge function (VISION capability), usePushNotifications for permission flow, food search + custom_foods for validation
competitorRef: MacroFactor: voice parsing; MyFitnessPal: meal photo scanning; Whoop: voice quick-add
accuracyOrRisk: Medical liability: food weight estimation from photos has 10-20% variance. Mitigate with: show user estimated macros before confirming, link to portion estimation guide, terms: AI estimates are approximate; you are accountable.

gap: No carb-cycle adherence nudge or remainder visibility in daily log
whyItMatters: Carb cycling is baked into engine (training days high-carb, rest days low-carb). But daily log hides carb target and cycle phase — user sees only 'C 250g' with no context whether today is high or low. MacroFactor, RP coaching show cycle context. Weak adherence on cut's most constraining macro (carbs on rest days) means users blow deficit or feel arbitrary restriction.
proposedFill: In daily log's macro-bars section: add 'training day / rest day' label + carb-cycling context line ('Low-carb: 150g carbs on rest' or 'Workout fuel: 300g carbs + 60g dextrose'). Show which macros are engine-set vs. profile default (teal ENGINE-SET badge already exists). Add carb remainder as a third ring or micro-bar so it's equally visible as calorie/protein (tie to aggressive-cut rules: rest days = 0 carbs outside dairy/veg).
leveragesInfra: useDailyTargets hook already knows training-day status via athlete_state + program schedule; MacroGoalsEditor section-label logic; existing Fuel tab tab-switching for context
competitorRef: MacroFactor: cycle phase callout in daily summary; Renaissance Periodization: carb timing color-coded
accuracyOrRisk: low risk

gap: No easy way to log a full recent day (copy-yesterday) for travel/consistent days
whyItMatters: On travel, athletes often eat exact same meals for 2-3 days. Manual re-entry of 8-12 items per day is 2+ minutes of friction. Copy-yesterday feature lets them tap once and adjust portions. MacroFactor, FatSecret have this. It removes a significant friction point for adherence during unstructured travel days.
proposedFill: Add 'Copy Previous Day' button in sticky action bar (desktop) or More sheet (mobile) that pre-fills all food_entries from yesterday into selected date with same portions and meal types. Show preview dialog: list of foods + totals, with 'Adjust' button for quick re-scaling (e.g., scale all by 1.1x for higher TDEE). Mark all as not-yet-logged (planned: false) so they count immediately toward today's log.
leveragesInfra: foodEntries query already fetches by date; SelectionDialog + form reuse from existing Meal-Add pattern; calculateMacros to preview totals
competitorRef: MacroFactor, FatSecret, MyFitnessPal: one-tap copy-yesterday
accuracyOrRisk: low risk

gap: No post-workout macro reminder or pre-planned quick meals triggered by completed workouts
whyItMatters: Carb timing on training days is critical for recovery (protein + fast carbs immediately post-lift). But users often forget or don't know 'I just finished a 60-min session, I need my post-workout window food.' Garmin sync already logs workout completion in real-time. A push notification + in-app quick-meal picker (pre-built meal templates filtered for post-workout timing) would close adherence gap for most time-sensitive macro window.
proposedFill: Hook on garmin-activities-sync completion: if activity is strength/lifting (activity_type=STRENGTH_TRAINING), trigger send-reminder-push variant that says 'Post-workout window open — tap for quick meal options' + in-app modal showing meal_templates filtered by timing=post in their ingredients, ranked by macro fit to today's remaining carb+protein targets. User taps one, 1-2 clicks logs whole meal. Integrate with existing MealTemplates apply-dialog UX.
leveragesInfra: garmin-sync edge function, send-reminder-push function (already exists), MealTemplates apply-dialog flow, meal_templates.meals.timing attribute already tracks this
competitorRef: WHOOP: post-workout fuel reminder + suggested meals; Peloton: in-app post-class recovery nutrition
accuracyOrRisk: low risk: notification is a suggestion, user controls confirmation

gap: No restaurant/branded restaurant menu integration for eating out
whyItMatters: USDA + Open Food Facts give good generic + packaged brand coverage, but restaurant chains (Chipotle, Olive Garden, Subway, local restaurants) require manual entry or internet search outside the app. This forces friction during the meal when user has no time to hunt for macro values. Eating out 2-3x/week (typical for professional athletes) means 20-30% of logging sessions require manual estimation. Elite coaches use restaurant menu integrations.
proposedFill: Add restaurant-chain autocomplete to food search: integrate Nutritionix API (free tier) for major chains + local restaurant menus when available. If search hits Nutritionix entry, surface it with brand logo + 'Restaurant' tag to distinguish from generic. Fall back to USDA/OFF if no restaurant hit. Build restaurant-meals custom_foods sync: users bookmark favorite restaurant meals; system stores them with brand_name + restaurant metadata so 'Chipotle chicken bowl' is always 1 tap away next time.
leveragesInfra: usda.js proxy pattern (extend to route Nutritionix API calls via edge function for auth/rate-limit); custom_foods table already has brand_name column; searchGenericFoods + searchBrandedFoods patterns
competitorRef: MyFitnessPal Nutritionix integration; MacroFactor restaurant menu; Cronometer restaurant search
accuracyOrRisk: Moderate: restaurant nutrition data is source-dependent (Nutritionix is crowdsourced, may have ±15% variance). Mitigate with: disclaimer badge on restaurant entries, encourage user to verify portion visually, option to flag if data was off.

gap: No intra-day macro deviation alerts when user is trending away from targets mid-day
whyItMatters: Users currently see only end-of-day totals. But on a cut, user might log breakfast + lunch at 4pm and already be 40% over on fats or under protein. By waiting until evening to recognize miss, there's no time to course-correct. Elite coaching apps flag mid-day drift so users can adjust dinner. This is difference between -5% vs 0% adherence day.
proposedFill: Add optional Intra-day Coach nudge (toggle in NotificationSettings): at 2pm and 5pm, check today's logged meals against remaining budget. If any macro is >20% away from proportional target, send push notification with summary + suggestion. Show temporary in-app banner (dismissible, not modal) when user opens FoodTracker. Use same MacroFiller logic to suggest foods.
leveragesInfra: NotificationSettings + usePushNotifications, send-reminder-push variant, useDailyTargets + calculateMacros (nutritionUtils), existing banner/toast patterns
competitorRef: MacroFactor: mid-day logging nudge (optional); Whoop: real-time adherence alerts
accuracyOrRisk: low risk: alerts are informational, not prescriptive

gap: No recipe scaling UI with ingredient-level portion adjustments
whyItMatters: RecipeBuilder exists but has usability trap: scaling a recipe to X servings scales all ingredients uniformly. But real cooking often requires tweaking individual ingredients (e.g., double the protein, keep carbs same). Users end up deleting recipes and building custom meals manually, losing time-save benefit. Elite meal-prep systems let you scale ingredients independently.
proposedFill: In RecipeBuilder's log dialog: after user selects serving count, show 'Adjust Individual Ingredients' disclosure. Each ingredient appears as slider or input field (like MacroGoalsEditor does for macros) with current grams + macro contribution shown live. User can drag/type to adjust each without recalculating whole recipe. Macros update real-time. When confirmed, adjusted recipe is stored as variant in same recipe.ingredients array or as new adapted recipe fork to preserve original.
leveragesInfra: rescaleIngredient + stripBaseFields utilities (already written); RecipeBuilder's ingredient loop; existing slider/input patterns from MacroGoalsEditor
competitorRef: Mealime, Eat This Much: ingredient-level scaling
accuracyOrRisk: low risk: user controls all values, macros are auto-computed

gap: Exercise reorder mid-session (CONFIRMED MISSING from memory): Athletes cannot reorder exercises while logging — strict linear prescription order only. Adaptive engine learns from exercises but cannot adapt the sequence.
whyItMatters: At $10k/mo, elite coaches adapt session flow on the fly based on recovery, energy, and equipment availability. OptiGains locks the athlete into the prescribed order even if (e.g.) a barbell squat rack is unexpectedly occupied mid-session. This breaks trust in adaptability and forces wasteful substitutions or session abandonment.
proposedFill: Drag-to-reorder exercises within ExerciseCard list (mirrors ProgramBuilder's @dnd-kit usage). Reorder events log to session notes as PRE/POST blocks so the engine's notes_parser.py can learn that the athlete habitually swaps exercises X↔Y when Z is unavailable, and adjust weekly programming accordingly. No UI cruft — swipe handle in the exercise header (hidden by default, revealed on long-press or hover).
leveragesInfra: @dnd-kit/core (already installed for ProgramBuilder), useWorkoutExercises (extend with reorder callback), session notes + notes_parser (already learning from notes).
accuracyOrRisk: low risk
competitorRef: Hevy, MacroFactor allow mid-workout exercise reorder; Whoop/CalAI do not

gap: No set-by-set autoregulation after a logged set. Athletes log RIR/RPE but receive zero in-session guidance to adjust load for the next set (e.g., 'RIR=1 on Set 2 → drop 10 lbs for Set 3').
whyItMatters: Autoregulation (adjusting weight per set based on rep speed, RPE, or RIR) is the foundation of high-intensity, high-frequency programming. Without it, athletes guess: too heavy = grind to failure and eat into recovery budget; too light = wasted volume that doesn't drive adaptation. Results stall because load isn't rising on the right sets. At elite pricing, this is a critical coaching gap.
proposedFill: When RIR is logged on a completed set, compare against performance bands (e.g., RIR 3-2 = maintain, RIR 1 = raise 2.5 lbs next set, RIR 0 = drop 5 lbs). Render inline suggestion chip after set completion: 'RIR 1 — consider +2.5 lbs for your next set' with one-tap apply. Route suggestion to next set's weight field. Sync with evaluateSetPerformance (program mode) + getBetweenSetCoaching (free mode) — extend their logic to include load adjustments, not just messaging.
leveragesInfra: getBetweenSetCoaching (Phase 3), evaluateSetPerformance, ExerciseCard coaching chip UI (already renders between-set messages), onApplyCoachingSuggestion callback.
accuracyOrRisk: low risk — science-backed (RPE/RIR scaling is standard; no medical claims)
competitorRef: Hevy: advanced autoregulation engine; RP Coaching App: detailed load nudges; Whoop: does not provide set-by-set autoregulation

gap: Pre-session readiness gate missing: No 'How do you feel?' check-in before starting a session. Engine receives MorningCheckin (energy/mood) but the logging UI does not prompt or gate the session start on readiness, nor does it surface that data to the athlete mid-logging.
whyItMatters: Elite coaches check in before every session to calibrate intensity and volume (e.g., low energy → reduce volume 20%, stay high intensity). OptiGains does nothing with morning readiness at logging time. Session prescription is locked in regardless of how the athlete wakes up. This ignores one of the highest-ROI coaching interventions and makes the app feel impersonal/robotic.
proposedFill: Before 'Start Logging' is clickable, surface an optional inline 'quick check-in': 1-10 energy slider + 'any notes?' text box (2 seconds to answer). If energy < 5, show a calm advisory: 'Low energy — consider dropping sets or reps by 1-2 today; recovery still counts.' Pass check-in data into session notes (PRE: energy=X, notes=Y) so notes_parser.py learns the engine can modulate programming based on daily readiness. Do NOT auto-adjust prescription — just surface the data and let the athlete decide.
leveragesInfra: MorningCheckin component (readiness logic model), session notes + notes_parser (already parsing), PreSessionInsightCard (UX pattern for inline coaching). New: simple energy input (reuse MorningCheckin's NumberPicker), optional gate dialog.
accuracyOrRisk: low risk — subjective data only, mirrors standard coaching practice
competitorRef: Whoop: mandatory readiness gate before workouts; MacroFactor: optional pre-meal check-in; RP: no readiness gate

gap: Plate calculator is buried in CalculatorsModal (mobile: tap Layout → ???). Not surfaced in logging UI — athlete must flip between the logging screen and calculator app to load the bar. Mobile-first app (per memory) but calculator is unreachable mid-set.
whyItMatters: Live barbell logging requires fast plate math (target weight → bars + plates). Making the athlete leave the logging screen kills flow and introduces tab-switch friction. At sub-10-rep, high-load movements, wrong loads are common and cost 2-3 minutes to recalculate. Elite coaching should make this frictionless.
proposedFill: Add a contextual 'Plate Calculator' button in the set row when an input is focused (appears after weight input is tapped, sits inline or as a popover). Clicking opens a fast plate-calc sheet (not a full modal — a bottom sheet on mobile) with the current set weight pre-filled as the target. Pre-populate bar weight from athlete's profile (standard 45 lbs / 20 kg by default, customizable). One-tap close to return to logging. No navigation away.
leveragesInfra: CalculatorsModal (copy PlateCalculator logic), useProfile (bar weight pref), inline popover/sheet UI (use existing Dialog or bottom-sheet component).
accuracyOrRisk: low risk
competitorRef: Hevy: plate calc available mid-logging; MacroFactor: does not apply (nutrition); Whoop: does not apply

gap: Exercise swap (replace) does not preserve set-by-set progress when an athlete discovers mid-session that the prescribed exercise is unavailable. Swapping resets all sets to set_number=1 and clears completed flags, losing partial progress on that exercise.
whyItMatters: Real workouts have constraints: bars occupied, machines broken, or (e.g.) an athlete who blocked Trap Bar Squat (per exercise_preferences) still gets it prescribed. A mid-session swap should carry over 'I already did 2 hard sets of the previous exercise' → let me do 1 more on the replacement.' Instead, swap → loss of record → demoralizing. Breaks trust in adaptability.
proposedFill: When replaceExercise is called (from the ExerciseCard menu or via the swap dialog), carry forward completed set count: if the athlete completed N sets before the swap, initialize the replacement with N sets pre-marked completed and the (N+1)th set as the active target. Preserve set numbers (don't renumber to 1). This reads as 'I got my working sets in, now finishing on this movement.' Pair with session notes: PRE: 'Swapped Trap Bar Squat → Goblet Squat after 2 sets' so the engine knows equipment constraints.
leveragesInfra: replaceExercise (useWorkoutExercises), ExerciseCard (no UI change needed), session notes.
accuracyOrRisk: low risk
competitorRef: Hevy: swap loses history; RP: does not apply

gap: Rest timer is agnostic to bar load and movement type. getSmartRestDuration returns ~180s compound / ~90s isolation, but no micro-adjustment for intensity. Heavy singles (1×5 squats) need ~3-4 min; lighter back-off work needs 45s. Also, rest timer dies when user tabs away (not absolute-timestamp-based mid-session, only in rest-tick loop).
whyItMatters: High-intensity, high-frequency programming demands precise rest intervals to preserve neurological state (CNS fatigue). Undershooting rest = incomplete motor-unit recovery = next set's RIR/load drops unexpectedly. Overshooting = program drags. At $10k/mo, rest should be coached, not guessed. Also, backgrounding the app kills the timer UX — phone call comes in, athlete tabs back to logging, timer is dead. Perceived unreliability erodes trust.
proposedFill: Extend getSmartRestDuration to accept set context: weight + reps + prev RIR. If (weight > 85% e1rm && reps <= 3) → 3m rest; if (weight < 60% e1rm && reps >= 8) → 60s. For the dead-timer bug: startRestTimer already uses absolute end timestamp (restTimerEndRef), but needs to survive tab loss. Re-tick on visibilitychange + focus events (already re-ticks in 500ms intervals, so should be fine — verify this doesn't regress in WorkoutDetail). Add optional coach message: 'Rest 3m for heavy compound — you'll want it.'
leveragesInfra: getSmartRestDuration, startRestTimer (WorkoutDetail + QuickWorkout both already use absolute timestamps), visibilitychange / focus events (browser APIs).
accuracyOrRisk: low risk — rest timing is well-studied; no medical claims
competitorRef: Whoop: adaptive rest timers (wearable-based); Hevy: static per-exercise rest, no load adjustment; RP: coach-set rest, not algorithmic

gap: No superset or exercise grouping support. Athletes cannot mark exercises as paired/antagonistic (e.g., Bench → Incline Press, or Leg Curl ↔ Leg Extension superset). Engine sees them as isolated exercises, not a block.
whyItMatters: High-intensity, high-frequency, low-volume protocols often use antagonist supersets (chest/back on same set, biceps/triceps pairs) to save time and preserve CNS. OptiGains treats each exercise independently, so the engine cannot learn that 'when athlete logs Bench + Incline as a pair, total chest load is X' — it counts them as separate, unrelated efforts. Programming precision suffers.
proposedFill: Optional 'Pair with previous' toggle in ExerciseCard header (visible only when ≥2 exercises logged). When enabled, render both exercises in a grouped card with shared set rows (e.g., Set 1: Bench A × B, Incline A' × B', rest 60s, repeat). Store pair metadata in exercises[i].paired_with = exercises[i-1].name. Notes_parser learns '(Bench × Incline) pair' blocks. This is a larger feature — start MVP: just mark pairing, render in a collapsed group, log separately but tag in notes. Do NOT implement full superset row UI in this pass.
leveragesInfra: ExerciseCard UI, session notes + notes_parser, useWorkoutExercises (extend to track pairing).
accuracyOrRisk: low risk — logging is still per-exercise, pairing is metadata only
competitorRef: Hevy: full superset support; MacroFactor: does not apply; RP Coaching: superset notation in PDF, not live

gap: No 'quick re-log last session' flow. Athlete must manually add every exercise + set count from scratch, even if they're repeating the exact same session (common with periodized programs). Lookup is automatic (autofill load/reps from history), but no 'Load last session' button to bypass the form.
whyItMatters: Periodized programs repeat the same workout 2-4 times per microcycle. Re-logging from scratch (type exercise name, click Add, add sets, fill reps) is friction every time. Elite coaching removes friction for high-frequency actions. With 3 exercises × 3 sets × 2 sessions/week, that's 36 taps/week of unnecessary input.
proposedFill: On the QuickWorkout + WorkoutDetail pages, if a user has logged the same workout title before (exact match), surface a floating chip above the empty exercise list: 'Repeat [Exercise Count] exercises from last time?' with one-tap Load button. Clicking pre-fills exercises, set counts, reps (from the most recent log of that session). Athlete adjusts load and logs. This mirrors the Resume Session flow (already in the UI) and re-uses the same chip pattern. Optional: keyboard shortcut or swipe gesture.
leveragesInfra: QuickWorkout + WorkoutDetail (both have 'resume session' flows to model from), allWorkoutLogs (already queried), AddExerciseForm.
accuracyOrRisk: low risk
competitorRef: Hevy: 'repeat last workout' button; MacroFactor: does not apply; Whoop: does not apply

gap: RIR / RPE input is optional and many free-workout athletes skip it. Between-set coaching (Phase 3) and autoregulation require RIR data, but no enforcement or gentle reminder to log it. Sets can be completed without any intensity metric.
whyItMatters: RIR/RPE is the linchpin for set-by-set autoregulation and coaching. If the athlete logs weight × reps but leaves RIR blank, the engine gets no signal. Phase 3 coaching becomes noise. At $10k/mo, every set should feed the learning loop. Weak adoption of RIR = weak coaching signal = poor results.
proposedFill: After a set is marked complete (checkbox tapped), auto-focus the RIR input with a subtle animation + inline label 'How many reps left in the tank?' so the athlete understands the purpose immediately. If they try to move to the next set WITHOUT filling RIR, show a gentle toast: 'RIR helps us coach the next set — take 2 seconds?' (not a hard block, just a nudge). On Phase 3+ accounts, show a coach chip: 'RIR 2 last set — suggest +5 lbs' to reinforce its value.
leveragesInfra: ExerciseCard (RIR input field, already exists), handleSetCompleted (add auto-focus logic), toast notifications.
accuracyOrRisk: low risk
competitorRef: Hevy: RPE optional, gentle reminder post-set; RP: RPE required; Whoop: does not apply

gap: Weekly Plan Rationale Not Surfaced to User
whyItMatters: The allocator writes a human-readable 'rationale' (why this week's volume split, why muscles got this many sets, what constraint drove the allocation) but it never reaches the UI. The athlete has no visibility into WHETHER the engine is spending budget intelligently or IF the targets make sense for their goals/recovery. At $10k/mo, the coach explains every decision; opacity erodes trust.
proposedFill: Weekly Plan Rationale card on the WeeklySchedule page, right under the 'Weekly Volume' breakdown. Show: (1) muscleVolume totals per muscle, (2) rationale text from weekly_plans.rationale, (3) recovery-budget scalar (TSB influence, cut phase). If no plan exists, surface "plan will generate Sunday night." Tap the card to drill into the per-muscle goal weights (strength/hypertrophy/PST priority × deadline urgency × learned muscle emphasis).
leveragesInfra: weekly_plans table (rationale field already written by allocator), WeeklySchedule.jsx already shows muscleVolume + reads weekly_plans, existing Card + disclosure pattern for expansions

gap: Progression Transparency — No "Why This Load" Explanation
whyItMatters: ProgramDetail.jsx shows 'ready_to_progress' badges and 'stalled' warnings, but NOT WHY the app prescribed *this specific load*. The prescription algorithm (strength_progression.py) computes daily_min_pct (floor), max_increment, readiness attenuation — none of it surfaces. Athlete wonders: "Is this too conservative? Too aggressive? Did I plateau or did the app hold me back?" Kills trust in the system's judgment.
proposedFill: Tap any exercise in the Progression Tracking card to reveal a 1-line explanation: "185 lbs (daily min: 165@85%, last 5d avg RIR: 1.2, so +5 lbs available). Last week 6 sets, this week target 8 (responding well — MEV funded first)." Show min weight, reasoning for increment, sets progress, deviation from plan if any.
leveragesInfra: enrollment.progression_state already holds working_weight, sessions_at_current_weight, last_session_rir_avg; strength_progression.py + daily_min_pct logic; existing detail modal (WorkoutDetail) can be adapted

gap: No Surface-Level Stall-vs-Plateau Detection + Actionable Guidance
whyItMatters: The 'stalled' badge on an exercise is a 1-bit signal (yes/no). But a coach asks: stalled 1 week (noise) or 3 weeks (pattern)? Fatigue-driven (RIR spike, soreness high) or intensity ceiling (hit same weight 5 sessions, now just louder — form limit, not recovery)? The current failure_reason capture ("systemic" eases the cut, "technical" stays hard) is the lever, but it's buried in the logged-session workflow and never feeds back to the Progression card. No closed loop: athlete marks "grip strength" as the sticking point, the engine doesn't know to deprioritize bench or suggest accommodations.
proposedFill: When an exercise stalls for 2+ weeks, show a diagnostic card: "Bench Press stalled 2 weeks. Last 6 sessions: RIR avg 0.8 (near-failure), soreness avg 3/5 (moderate). Likely: strength ceiling or form breakdown, not underrecovery. Suggestion: drop to 5-rep target 1 week to reset groove, then try RPE-based work." Consume failure_reason tags logged during session, surface to the coach/UI, and let the brief or prescription adapt.
leveragesInfra: failure_reason data already logged in workout_logs; notes_parser.py already parses caution/stalling; existing ProgramDetail stall_suggestion field can be populated by a new learner that aggregates failure_reason tags + RIR trends

gap: Exercise-Value Feedback Loop Invisible to User
whyItMatters: The learner (learners.update_exercise_value) tracks which exercises the athlete chooses, skips, rates, and learns "this barbell row produces more e1RM slope than dumbbell row for you." But the user never sees this. They can't learn what the app learned (e.g., "Leg Press [+0.8 value, 60% confidence] outgains Hack Squat [−0.2, 40%] for you"). Without seeing the learned hierarchy, they can't course-correct the training philosophy if the app is wrong, and they don't build the mental model that shapes future input.
proposedFill: Persistence page (or sub-tab in Progress) showing per-exercise value scores: "Bench Press +2.1 [grown 12 wks], Incline DB +0.3 [still learning], Decline Press −0.5 [high fatigue cost, low ROI]." Color by confidence (unfaded if mature, faded if immature). Show the data points: e1RM slope, sessions logged, # times chosen vs offered. Let user upvote/downvote to supply explicit preference feedback (override or refine the learned signal).
leveragesInfra: athlete_params table (exercise_values meta), learners.exercise_value() already computes the posterior, notes_parser.py feeds sentiment + too_easy/too_hard, session_generator already uses exercise_values in _priority_score

gap: No Adaptive Engine Control Panel — Can't See Why Next Session Was Built This Way
whyItMatters: The allocator runs weekly, the session generator runs daily, but the user has no dashboard showing: "Your weekly budget is 68 sets (was 72, cut phase −10%, TSB +1% from recovery). Focused on chest [+40% deadline urgency, 11 wks to PST], normal on everything else. This session: 4 lifting + 1 cardio [recovery =LIGHT, readiness −12% from poor HRV]. Next: back focus [recovery credit from strength carry-over]." A $10k/mo coach narrates the plan daily; a $0/mo training app should show it on demand.
proposedFill: New card in AthleteState page or a floating '?' icon on WeeklySchedule: "Daily Plan Breakdown." Shows: (1) weekly budget decomposition (base Σ MAV, recovery scalar, phase scalar), (2) how muscles are prioritized this week (goal weights), (3) today's capacity (action class, readiness attenuation, soreness trim), (4) selected exercises (why these 5, not the other 8 candidates — learned value, goal priority, fatigue cost order). Expand each section to see the math or the candidate list.
leveragesInfra: allocator.py already computes all these values; training_prescription + athlete_state jsonb holds capacity; session_generator has exercise scoring; existing expandable Card + disclosure pattern (used in WeeklySchedule for volume)

gap: Controlled Test Scheduler Invisible; User Can't Opt-In or See Test Progress
whyItMatters: The design doc specifies 6 test types (recovery_stress, volume_tolerance, running_tolerance, pst_diagnostic) that systematically learn MRV, frequency, and recovery capacity. But controlled_tests table exists and is never shown to the user. They don't know a test is running, don't understand why their plan changed ("Why am I suddenly doing 6 sets of chest instead of 4?"), and can't give informed consent (necessary for medical/liability trust). Without visibility, the athlete feels the engine is experimenting on them, not with them.
proposedFill: "Controlled Tests" section in AthleteState or ProgramDetail. Shows active test (if any): "Volume-Tolerance Test: Chest (Weeks 3–5). Ramping volume +2 sets/wk to find your MRV. Track soreness + e1RM slope — if stall+soreness, we'll deload. Purpose: optimize your program once we know your true ceiling." Show scheduled tests, completed tests (result + what was learned). Let user postpone a test or request one ("I think my lats can handle more").
leveragesInfra: controlled_tests table (test_type, status, baseline, result, rationale fields); learners.py has the observation logic; existing Card + timeline pattern

gap: Program Deviation Tracking Not Surfaced — Prescribed vs Actual Volume Blind Spot
whyItMatters: If the allocator prescribed 4 sets of chest but the athlete logged 2 (soreness, schedule, boredom, form breakdown), the weekly_plans target is now stale. The engine should flag this deviation (and why — notes capture form caution, soreness, time pressure) so it can adjust next week. Right now it's silent. The brief mentions "you're under-recovering" but never says "you logged half the prescribed volume Thursday (why?) so Friday's targets compensated." At elite level, this feedback loop — "here's what you did vs plan, here's why the engine adapted" — is *the* coaching signal.
proposedFill: On WeeklySchedule, add a small data bar under "Weekly Volume": "Planned 72 sets, logged 68 (94%). Chest −2 (logged soreness Tue), Back +3 (felt strong). Engine adjusted Friday targets to keep total recovery budget." Tap to see per-day deviation (planned vs logged, reason if flagged). This teaches the athlete that the engine reads their log and *responds*, not just prescribes.
leveragesInfra: weekly_plans (set_targets), workout_logs (per-day sets + notes), deviation_tracker.py already exists, failure_reason + notes parsing in place; WeeklySchedule already calculates muscleVolume from programEntries

gap: Personalization Maturity Not Visible — User Doesn't Know if Engine Has Learned Them Yet
whyItMatters: AthleteState.jsx shows "Personalization: Calibrating 2/4" (from rls_params.update_count), but that's DEPRECATED (per ADAPTIVE_ENGINE_DESIGN.md §7). The NEW maturity signal is athlete_landmarks.mature (per-muscle, based on credible-interval separation after 8+ weeks). A user 4 weeks in should know: "Your chest MRV is still a population guess; your quads are personalized (found your ceiling after stalling + recovering)." This tells them when the engine is finally *actually coaching them* vs just running a template.
proposedFill: Maturity Summary card in AthleteState: "Personalization: 4 of 11 muscles personalized (learned your real MRV, not a guess). Mature: Chest [N=12 weeks], Quads [N=9 weeks]. Still calibrating: Lats, Hamstrings [need 4 more weeks data + responsiveness to mature]." Show per-muscle sliders or a grid. Tie to confidence in weekly_plans ("plan is 36% personalized" → can display in WeeklySchedule rationale).
leveragesInfra: athlete_landmarks table (mature, n_obs per muscle), allocator already computes plan confidence, learners.py §4 sets maturity rules

gap: Deviation Handling in Train Workflow — No Feedback on "Why Did the Engine Give Me This Today?"
whyItMatters: Train.jsx → WeeklySchedule shows the prescribed session + a "Start Session" CTA, but the athlete never sees the reasoning for TODAY's specific breakdown. They log 3 pull-ups instead of 5 prescribed, soreness hits, and next session's targets shift — but the brief or session gen doesn't SAY "your pull count was down yesterday, so we backed off today's upper volume." At $10k/mo, the coach explains deviation handling and volume rebalancing; the app should do the same at the moment of use (not buried in a debug panel).
proposedFill: Small collapsible section on each prescribed session card in WeeklySchedule: "Today's Plan: 4 lift + 1 cardio. Capacity: [readiness icon] Good recovery (HRV +8, RHR 52, sleep 7.5h), TSB +3 (fresh). Agenda: Chest focus [deadline +15 days to PST]. Volume adjusted from planned (expected 5 lift yesterday, logged 3 + soreness ache) so today prioritizes recovery while keeping chest work." This makes the session feel CHOSEN (adaptive) not IMPOSED (rigid).
leveragesInfra: WeeklySchedule already reads readiness metrics (HRV, RHR, sleep via athlete_state), session_generator has capacity class, deviation_tracker calculates deviation, existing session cards in WeeklySchedule can be expanded

gap: Sleep + HRV → session load adjustment missing. Recovery data (HRV, sleep, ACWR) is DISPLAYED in RecoveryDetail but NEVER feeds back into session prescription. Low HRV + poor sleep still get the same prescribed load; no downregulation signal reaches the daily prescriber.
whyItMatters: Elite coaching adjusts INTENSITY and VOLUME in real-time based on morning readiness. A $10k/mo coach reads low HRV (stress accumulation) + sleep debt and reduces prescribed RIR (increases difficulty slightly to prevent overreach) or cuts a cardio session entirely. Without this loop, the athlete trains blind—Banister confidence drops because compliance becomes random.
proposedFill: Add recovery_budget_adjustment() edge function that reads daily HRV z-score + sleep_debt_7d_hours + body_battery from recovery_metrics + athlete_state, computes a load-modifier (0.8–1.0 for 70+ readiness, 0.6–0.8 for <50), and writes to training_prescription.load_adjustment. Daily prescriber reads this and lowers RIR floor (soften the prescribed difficulty gate, delay harder variations by 1 day). Display the adjustment reason in PrescribedSessionCard (e.g., 'Load reduced: low HRV + 5h sleep debt').
leveragesInfra: Uses existing recovery_metrics + athlete_state (compute_athlete_state.py already computes HRV z-score, sleep_debt, body_battery); extends training_prescription table with load_adjustment JSONB. Uses existing Kalman confidence and overreach_signal to gate severity.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Adjustment is TRANSPARENT in UI; athlete can override or ignore. No medical claims—strictly operational (e.g., 'lower difficulty gate today' is not 'rest means you're broken'). Pattern validated by TrainHeroic/Whoop/MacroFactor.

gap: Soreness → volume routing disconnected. MorningCheckin captures per-muscle soreness (snapshot stored in daily_readiness + soreness_logs rows), but the daily prescriber never consults it when assigning WHICH muscles train today. High soreness in quads still gets quads prescribed; no intelligent avoidance.
whyItMatters: Soreness-guided autoregulation is a core RPE-coach pattern: sore quads = skip squat variation OR do leg press (lower eccentric damage) instead. This teaches the athlete the difference between 'muscle is fatigued' (sore = ready for volume when weight is right) and 'nervous system overreached' (soreness + low HRV = back off). Improves adherence because the daily plan ADAPTS to the body instead of demanding a fixed schedule.
proposedFill: Extend session_generator (or daily prescriber orchestrator) to read soreness_logs for today, identify high-soreness muscles (level ≥2), and shuffle exercises: prefer accessory ↔ main lift substitution (e.g., if high soreness in quads, offer tempo/pausedLeg Press instead of Squat comp for the day), OR demote that muscle-group session to lighter RPE/RIR. Write soreness_rationale to training_prescription.adjustments_notes. Surface in PrescribedSessionCard: '(quads sore; swap to paused leg press)'.
leveragesInfra: Reads soreness_logs table (already written by MorningCheckin); re-uses exercise substitution logic from engine.muscle_map and program_builder. Writes to training_prescription.adjustments_notes (already exists as JSONB).
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Swap logic is conservative (same muscle group, lower eccentric load); athlete always sees the override reason and can manually select original exercise. No medical claim—'soreness → variation' is standard coaching pattern.

gap: Recovery budget band visibility and adaptive allocation gap. compute_athlete_state.py computes recovery components (HRV, sleep debt, ACWR, TSB) and guards overreach detection, but recovery_budget itself is never DISPLAYED to the athlete or fed to a volume allocator. They see TSB/ACWR numbers but not 'you have 2 more hard days left this week' or 'ease next 3 days'.
whyItMatters: Adherence comes from understanding WHY a session is light or skipped. MacroFactor users see 'deficit room remaining', elite strength coaches manage 'fatigue room'. Without transparency, the athlete perceives downregulation as arbitrary ('Why's my session easier?') instead of principled ('I had 3 poor sleeps + low HRV—system is protecting my gains.'). Builds trust and compliance.
proposedFill: Compute weekly_recovery_budget from TSB target band (e.g., -5 to +10 TSB is goal; if at -15, budget 3 'ease days' to recover), HRV trend (3-consecutive-drops = fast-track back to baseline), and sleep debt (>8h = 1 full easy day per 8h). Write to athlete_state.recovery_budget as {days_remaining, reason_summary, hard_day_cap, ease_day_floor}. Surface in RecoveryDetail as a new card: 'Weekly Budget: 2 hard days left · 2 ease days to recover sleep debt.' This replaces the need for manual deload—the athlete sees the budget and self-regulates.
leveragesInfra: Uses existing TSB, HRV z-score, sleep_debt (all in athlete_state); Banister confidence gates whether to trust the budget. Extends athlete_state with recovery_budget JSONB.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Budget is advisory (not a hard-coded rule change); athlete can override in UI. Formula is conservative (favors recovery). Transparent display means no surprises.

gap: Post-workout supplement timing prompts absent. Supplement log exists (tables: supplement_types, supplement_logs), and the daily brief hints at recovery, but no time-locked reminders (e.g., 30min post-lift: 'Log creatine + carbs now for glycogen window'). Recovery stack adherence is invisible to the system.
whyItMatters: Supplement timing (creatine, carbs, amino acids, minerals post-workout) is a direct knob on Kalman input (affects fatigue clearance via nutrition_modulator). If the athlete logs supplements inconsistently, the system can't learn their baseline or trust trends. Elite programs front-load 'take X now' urgency—the brief says 'log it' but doesn't PUSH the notification at the golden minute.
proposedFill: After session_complete webhook fires (post-workout), send push notification 'Post-workout window open (30 min): log your carbs + creatine?' with deep link to Supplements tab pre-filled with 'Post-Workout Stack' template (reads supplement_types for records with post_workout_timing=true). Use existing send-reminder-push edge function and usePushNotifications hook. Log which supplements were taken and at what time offset to session end; feed offset into nutrition_modulator's macro absorption window.
leveragesInfra: Re-uses send-reminder-push edge function (already deployed); extends supplement_logs with timing_seconds_post_session. Reads supplement_types.post_workout_timing boolean (define once). Integration point: after workout_logs upsert.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Notification is optional; athlete can dismiss. Medical/liability: frame as 'convenience reminder' not 'required for health'. Supplement claims already disclaimed in Supplements.jsx.

gap: Wind-down and sleep hygiene protocol missing. Morning check-in captures sleep DURATION and QUALITY (sleep_score) but no prompts BEFORE bed. No 'lights out at 10:30pm' reminder, no 'avoid caffeine after 2pm' protocol linked to next morning's sleep outcome, no pre-bed supplement window (magnesium, L-theanine).
whyItMatters: Sleep debt half-fills the recovery valve on a cut (compute_athlete_state.py line 1294 tracks consecutive poor nights). Without a behavioral protocol to improve sleep, the system just watches it fail and eases calories reactively. Elite athletes ENGINEER sleep (consistent wind-down, no screens, controlled room). A $10k/mo coach texts 'no caffeine after 1pm today + 10:30pm lights out' → next morning's HRV is 8% higher → $300+ in better session adaptation.
proposedFill: Create wind-down protocol in a new evening_readiness table: stores user's target sleep time, caffeine cutoff (e.g., 2pm), pre-bed supplement stack (magnesium dose + timing). Daily send-reminder-push at 'target-time minus 90min' with message 'Wind down: no caffeine after {cutoff} · log pre-bed stack at {time}.' Link to a lightweight 'Pre-bed' card in Supplements tab (or new evening routine dialog). Next morning, compute sleep_quality_vs_protocol (did they follow the routine?) and feed into HRV confidence dampening; if protocol adherence is low, reduce TSB trust. Surface win/loss in RecoveryDetail: 'Last night: followed protocol ✓ → sleep 7.8h, HRV 52ms'.
leveragesInfra: Uses send-reminder-push (existing); extends supplement_logs with session_type='pre_bed' or timing_relative_to='lights_out'; reads user_profiles.target_sleep_time (define). Creates evening_readiness table (mirrors daily_readiness) to track adherence. Integrates with compute_athlete_state.py to weight HRV confidence by protocol follow.
accuracyOrRisk: Medical/liability: frame as 'sleep optimization tips' not 'sleep disorder treatment'. Tie caffeine cutoff to general wellness (e.g., 'caffeine half-life is 5–6h; 2pm cutoff gives 8-10h clear'), not medical claims. No diagnosis.

gap: No grip on WHICH recovery lever the system is pulling TODAY. When readiness is low (score <50) or ACWR is high (>1.3), the daily brief says 'ease' but doesn't specify: is it sleep debt? HRV overreach? Insufficient glycogen? This ambiguity means the athlete can't self-correct tomorrow (what do I change: sleep, carbs, volume, intensity?)
whyItMatters: Coaching transparency drives behavior change. 'Ease because sleep debt is 6h' → athlete prioritizes bed time. 'Ease because ACWR >1.3' → athlete prioritizes intensity-management or checks DOMS. Without attribution, 'ease' feels arbitrary or patronizing, risking adherence collapse and lost trust in the adaptive model.
proposedFill: Extend daily_brief generation in generate-daily-brief edge function to include recovery_diagnosis: identify the PRIMARY limiting factor (e.g., {factor: 'sleep_debt', value: 6, unit: 'hours', implication: 'prioritize 30min extra sleep tonight'}, {factor: 'acwr', value: 1.45, unit: 'ratio', implication: 'reduce intensity by 1 RIR across all lifts'}). Include in brief_json. Surface in DailyBriefCard as a mini-diagnosis row: 'Recovery gap: 5h sleep debt + elevated ACWR (1.4)' with expandable tips per factor. Also write to training_prescription.recovery_rationale so PrescribedSessionCard can show 'Load reduced (sleep debt + high load)' with a tap-to-expand 'why'.
leveragesInfra: Extends generate-daily-brief function (reads athlete_state.recovery); writes to daily_briefs.brief_json.recovery_diagnosis (JSONB). Uses existing AthleteState, no new tables.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Diagnosis is descriptive (not prescriptive); athlete can ignore. No medical claims—just factual reporting ('HRV declined 8ms' = HRV data, not 'you are overreached').

gap: No failure-to-recover escalation gate. If HRV drops 3 consecutive days + sleep <6h for 2+ nights + ACWR stays >1.3, the system detects overreaching (guardrail.check_overreaching() in compute_athlete_state.py) but merely SIGNALS it; no mandatory intervention. A manually-driven cut can still prescribe hard sessions when the flag is up.
whyItMatters: Overreaching is irreversible if the athlete keeps pushing through it (FINA studies show 4–12 week recovery cost). Elite systems have hard stops: 'You are overreached per multiple metrics; 48-hour full recovery required. Sessions locked.' OptiGains has the detection but no enforcement, making it advisory theater instead of protective.
proposedFill: When overreach_signal.overreaching==true, set training_prescription.override_lock={locked: true, reason: 'systemic_overreach', duration_hours: 48} in compute_athlete_state.py. PrescribedSessionCard checks this and renders: 'Recovery Mode Active — light session only (full rest encouraged). Unlock after 48h recovery or manually override if you accept the risk.' Unlock gated by: (current_time > locked_until) OR athlete taps 'I understand, proceed' (logs intent in a overreach_overrides table for audit). Do NOT auto-prescribe hard sessions during lock; default to mobility/breathing/easy walk.
leveragesInfra: Uses existing overreach_signal from guardrail module; extends training_prescription with override_lock JSONB. Adds overreach_overrides audit table. No new sensors needed.
accuracyOrRisk: Medical/liability: High caution. Framing is KEY—'Recovery mode activated per your physiological signals (HRV, sleep, load ratio)—this is protective, not restrictive.' Emphasize: athlete can override. Audit trail of overrides helps liability defense ('we warned them and they chose to continue'). Do NOT label as 'injury prevention' or 'medical advice'; use 'system is protecting your long-term progress.'
competitorRef: Whoop's Strain/Recovery locks; MacroFactor's 'stop eating deficit' gates; Biostrap's cardiac-drift shutdown.

gap: No direct feedback loop from workout OUTCOME → next day's prescribed load. A session goes hard (RIR 0, high CNS fatigue) but the athlete performs worse than expected (e.g., target 405×3 lands 395×2, or prescribed HR zone missed by 12 bpm), yet tomorrow's session ignores this signal. Kalman observation y_t comes from e1RM comparison to baseline (compute_observation_y), NOT from 'did the athlete actually hit the prescribed RIR/intensity today?'
whyItMatters: Form collapse mid-session signals CNS underrecovery. A coach sees 'benched 405 yesterday, hit 395×2 today despite full sleep' and reduces load 2 cycles early (prevents injury + trains the filter). Without this, the prescription engine assumes the session went to plan; the Kalman's observation only updates if the athlete's e1RM changed, which is slow and noisy. Missed readiness signals compound into overreach.
proposedFill: Add performance_check_log table with fields: {created_by, date, exercise, prescribed_reps, prescribed_rpe, prescribed_reps, actual_reps, actual_rpe, achieved_yes_no, form_quality, notes}. MorningCheckin or post-session card prompts 'Did you hit all the prescribed targets? (yes/mostly/no)' with a form-quality slider. If achieved=false or form_quality<7, log it. Modify compute_observation_y to consume these: if multiple consecutive days show actual_rpe > prescribed_rpe (form is slipping + effort is higher), weight the observation y_t downward (implies fatigue, not form). Feed into Kalman as a secondary observation stream, gated by confidence.
leveragesInfra: Extends workout_logs with performance_check details (or creates new performance_logs table). Modifies compute_observation_y function in compute_athlete_state.py. Uses existing Kalman step.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Athlete self-reports form quality (subjective but correlated with fatigue). Kalman gates by confidence—noisy input is down-weighted. No medical claim.

gap: No plateau/stall detection with predictive ETA and actionable breakout protocol
whyItMatters: Strength plateaus are the #1 adherence killer — athletes feel stuck and quit. A $10k coach surfaces stalls 1-2 weeks early (via regression slope + TSB state machine) and prescribes a specific 2-3 day deload + return pattern to re-sensitize. Currently the brief mentions stall_risk in strength JSON but NEVER tells Nolan what to do about it; he has to infer.
proposedFill: Add a Stall Monitor panel to Insights/AthleteState showing: (1) per-lift stall_risk + velocity trend, (2) ETA days to deload (auto-trigger at risk >= 0.6), (3) 1-click Activate Deload that modifies next 3 workout prescriptions (volume only, hold load). Surface in Insights as a red-badge card that only appears when risk >= 0.5.
leveragesInfra: athlete_state.strength[lift].{stall_risk, progression_rate_lbs_per_week, eta_days}; training_prescription.session_type already has LIGHT/DELOAD; daily brief prompt already fetches this data
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — stall_risk is a deterministic bandit UCB score computed by engine; athlete retains override control. Deload instruction aligns with training philosophy (downregulation = volume/RIR at held load).
competitorRef: RP (Renaissance Periodization) coaches prescribe explicit deload weeks; MacroFactor surfaces adherence fatigue

gap: No weekly synthesis or coach narrative — brief is daily only, brief history is flat list
whyItMatters: A $10k coach does Friday 10-min call: Here is the pattern I am seeing across the week, here is adherence vs plan, here is what we pivot. Daily briefs are noise without meta-narrative. Weekly synthesis ties together: adherence vs plan, volume cumulative trend, recovery trajectory, goal ETA, and prescribes next week's macro-strategy. This is where trust and retention live.
proposedFill: Create Weekly Coach Review (Sunday auto-gen via new edge function): (1) Adherence scorecard (sessions planned vs completed, tonnage vs target per muscle), (2) Recovery narrative (HRV/RHR 7d trend + interpretation), (3) Strength progression summary (e1RM changes per lift vs week-over-week), (4) ETA update (days to goal by lift), (5) Next-week adjustment (volume dial, intensity focus, conditioning pivot). Live at /weekly-review, linked from Insights.
leveragesInfra: athlete_state (daily snapshots, aggregate into weekly); recovery_metrics (7d window already available); workout_logs + workout_schedules (adherence math); training_prescription (weekly synthesis output); new edge function generate-weekly-review similar to generate-daily-brief structure
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — purely aggregation + narrative synthesis; no new computation. Uses existing athlete_state + recovery pipeline.
competitorRef: RP coaches, Whoop, Oura weekly summaries all have this; MacroFactor has compliance metric but not training-specific meta-narrative

gap: No trend storytelling for body composition — weight chart exists but no contextual narrative
whyItMatters: Nolan is cutting; weight trend is noisy (±0.5lb daily swings). A coach says: Your trend is minus 0.8 lb/wk on plan, adipose loss ~3 lbs this month, estimated 4 more weeks to 8% goal, strength maintenanced across all lifts = excellent cut execution. Without this, weight fluctuation causes false panic or complacency. Contextual narrative = adherence + confidence.
proposedFill: Expand Progress page Weight Tab to include: (1) Trend line (rolling 7d average, not raw daily), (2) Monthly stats (start/end weight, avg loss/gain per week, adipose estimate from physique entries if available), (3) Narrative: Phase progress + ETA to goal weight (uses diet_phases.target_weight + weight_trend_lbs_per_week), (4) Physiological signal (strength maintained? volume tolerated? = cut is sustainable). All computed server-side, surfaced as collapsible detail cards.
leveragesInfra: body_weight_entries (already logged); diet_phases.{target_weight, weekly_rate}; athlete_state.nutrition.{on_track, weight_trend}; physique_entries.bodyfat_estimate; useDailyTargets hook already available
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — narrative is client-side interpretation of existing logged data. No ML beyond existing trend calculation.
competitorRef: MacroFactor does this exceptionally well (trend line + narrative + adaptive calorie suggestion); Nolan already has the data, just not surfaced

gap: No ask-your-coach conversational mode — coaching intelligence is broadcast (daily brief) only, never interactive
whyItMatters: Nolan has a specific question at 3pm: Should I do a second session today? Can I push this muscle harder? Am I overtrained? A $10k coach is on-demand conversational. Currently he has to wait for tomorrow's brief or submit a form. Conversational coaching = perceived responsiveness + trust. Lower barrier to question asking = better adherence feedback loop.
proposedFill: Add Coach Chat tab to Coach page (below Coach Office Hours form review): Text input, send to new edge function ask-coach-question (streams Claude response with access to today's state, prescription, recovery, past 7d trend). Stores Q&A in new coach_qa table for pattern detection. Limited to 3 free questions/day (subscription upsell). Responses cite: today's readiness state, prescription rationale, risk flags.
leveragesInfra: Claude API (use existing Claude API key from brief generation); athlete_state, recovery_metrics, training_prescription, daily_readiness all queryable by function; new coach_qa table for audit trail and pattern learning.
accuracyOrRisk: Medium risk — conversational LLM can hallucinate or give contradictory advice vs daily brief. Mitigate: (1) always cite the data, (2) surface today's prescription prominently, (3) add disclaimers, (4) log all responses for audit.
competitorRef: Whoop has Whoop Coach (conversational); CalAI is conversational coaching core; no competitor does this at the daily-brief-integration level

gap: No accountability tracking: log adherence to prescribed actions, flag systemic misses
whyItMatters: The brief says: Do 3x squat session, eat 200g protein, run easy 3 miles. Nolan half-complies (skips run). Coach never knows he skipped it—there's no adherence signal tying prescribed_actions to actual_completion. A $10k coach confronts: You've skipped cardio 4 of last 6 weeks. What's the blocker? This is results-determining. Adherence tracking = the difference between a brief and a coaching relationship.
proposedFill: After each daily brief is generated, auto-create tasks from today_actions field and link them to workout_schedules + cardio_sessions. At end-of-day, compute adherence score (actions completed / actions prescribed). Store in new daily_adherence table. At weekly review, flag patterns: missed cardio, skipped strength sessions, under-target volume. Surface as weekly scorecard: Adherence X%, top miss pattern, 1-click coach explanation for why (excuse or legit blocker?). Coach can send follow-up nudge.
leveragesInfra: daily_briefs.brief_json.today_actions (already generated); workout_logs + cardio_sessions (already logged); daily_tasks table (materialized from templates, could extend to track prescribed actions); new daily_adherence table (date, created_by, planned, completed, score, top_miss).
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — pure aggregation logic, no personalized recommendation. Adherence is factual (did it or didn't). Flag is heuristic (3+ misses of type X) but coach can override.
competitorRef: MacroFactor tracks macro adherence aggressively; Whoop has compliance metric but only for prescribed sessions; RP coaches track workout adherence manually in spreadsheets.

gap: No exercise-specific reactive feedback loop — exercise_reactions logged but never fed back into brief or prescription
whyItMatters: Nolan logs: Back squat feels heavy/hard, bench press elbow tweaking. These are early warning signals for form breakdown, injury risk, or exercise tolerance. Currently exercise_reactions table exists but is never read. A $10k coach looks at the tape (form reviews) + the feel data and says: Stop benching, sub dumbbell press for 2 weeks, squat stances feeling tight = mobility work priority. Reactive adjustment = injury prevention + adherence (athlete doesn't feel ignored).
proposedFill: Extend generate-daily-brief function to read exercise_reactions from past 7 days and include as bullet point in performance coaching section: Flag high-severity reactions (tweaking/heavy/form-breakdown pattern), suggest: (1) form review (link to Coach office hours), (2) exercise substitute from exercise_preferences.preferred, (3) 2-week hypertrophy target adjustment to reduce that exercise. Make exercise reaction mandatory log (not optional) on any logged workout's post-note prompt.
leveragesInfra: exercise_reactions table (read-only); user_profiles.exercise_preferences (already honors blocked + preferred); daily brief function already generates performance section; form_reviews already exist as data source.
accuracyOrRisk: Low-medium risk — reaction is self-reported (subjective). Mitigate: (1) pattern detection (3+ consecutive high severity = flag, not single incident), (2) coach can override, (3) never auto-block exercise, only suggest review.
competitorRef: No competitor does this; most coaching is reactive (after injury). Novel for at-scale coaching.

gap: No goal ETA transparency or path confidence metric — goals exist but no live countdown
whyItMatters: Nolan's goal: PST 1.5mi sub-9:00. Today: his VDOT predicts 9:45 ETA. But when will he hit 9:00? In 8 weeks if adherence holds? In 12 if he misses running? A $10k coach has a real ETA and updates it weekly based on actual progress rate. This drives retention: athletes see progress momentum. Currently athlete_goals table exists but is never queried in the UI; no ETA, no confidence.
proposedFill: Add Goals Dashboard sub-page to Insights. For each active goal: (1) Show current value (e.g., 1.5mi time 9:45 from vdot_zones in athlete_state.endurance), (2) ETA days (extrapolate from 7d progression rate in athlete_state or training_prescription), (3) Confidence % (if VDOT improving trend is stable, confidence high; if volatile or missed sessions, lower), (4) Status bar (current % -> goal %). Auto-refresh when athlete_state updates. Link each goal to relevant coaching domain (PST -> endurance section of brief, etc.).
leveragesInfra: athlete_goals (read-only, already synced from second brain); athlete_state.{endurance, strength, nutrition} (all have ETAs computed per domain); vdot_zones in athlete_state; training_prescription.{mpc_action_scores, w_pst, w_str} (weights per goal).
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — ETA is extrapolation of existing trend data. If trend changes, ETA updates; athlete sees dynamic feedback. Confidence is heuristic (variance of trend over 14d window) but transparent.
competitorRef: Whoop has fitness tracking; MacroFactor has weight loss ETA; RP coaches manually estimate ETAs. Nolan already computes this internally, just not exposed.

gap: No recovery strategy optimization or sleep/HRV-linked session prescription adjustment
whyItMatters: Nolan has excellent wearable recovery data (HRV, RHR, body battery, sleep). This data arrives at 6am but the daily brief is generated the night before, so today's prescription is blind to recovery. A $10k coach sees 6am recovery metrics and says: HRV down 8%, body battery 35%, skip the AM conditioning, do strength-only today. Currently the prescription is rigid unless Nolan manually overrides. Mismatched recovery = burnout risk.
proposedFill: Modify generate-daily-brief function: (1) If called after 6am (has fresh recovery_metrics for today), include a Recovery Adjustment section: If recovery is low (HRV z-score < -1, body_battery < 40, sleep < 6h), auto-mod today's prescription (shift cardio from AM to evening optional, lower intensity floor from prescribed level). (2) Add toggle on daily brief to 'Adjust for today's recovery' (1-click downshift). (3) Log the adjustment in training_prescription for trend analysis.
leveragesInfra: recovery_metrics (synced daily from Garmin); daily_readiness (morning check-in already captures sleep_score); training_prescription already has mpc_intensity; banister_state in prescription already models fatigue.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — prescription downgrade is per his philosophy (reduce volume/intensity, hold load). Recovery data is objective (HRV z-score < -1 is a standard threshold). Athlete retains override.
competitorRef: Whoop does this via Whoop Coach (recovery-linked guidance); Oura Readiness score attempts this but integration is weak. Most platforms collect recovery data but don't reactively adjust prescription.

gap: No logging streak tracking or celebration — missed/skipped sessions have zero consequences or re-engagement trigger
whyItMatters: Streaks are the #1 habit-loop driver (psychology: identity-based behavior). Nolan's daily athletes LIVE on streaks. Missing a weigh-in, a physique check, or a daily readiness log breaks habit formation; no reward pathway for maintaining them = silent drop-off.
proposedFill: Add logging_streak table (user, metric_type='daily_readiness'|'weigh_in'|'physique'|'workout', current_streak, max_streak, last_logged_date, last_broken_date). Extend usePushNotifications with a post-notification celebration modal ("🔥 7-day logging streak!" + local confetti). Trigger re-engagement push 24h after a missed day: "Your streak was 14 days. Log today to restart."
leveragesInfra: push_subscriptions + send-daily-brief-push function (repurpose for celebration). Extends daily_readiness, physique_entries, body_weight_entries tables with streak metadata. Uses existing showLocalNotification hook.

gap: Physique check-in cadence is unguided — no smart reminder about WHEN to re-check based on phase/progress velocity
whyItMatters: Physique entries drive body-comp trust (the most visible form of adherence proof). But users log them randomly (once per month, or never after week 2). Coach pricing tier demands weekly physique checks on cuts to validate deficit adherence. Current push suite has no physique reminder, only generic weekly check-in.
proposedFill: Extend send-weekly-checkin-reminder to send-physique-checkin-reminder (new function). Logic: ON CUT phase & phase_start < 21 days ago → 3x/week Friday/Mon/Wed push "Your phase-progress briefing is ready — log your physique check (front/side/abs)." Include a 1-tap shortcut to PhysiqueTracker. Inherit user's phase from athlete_state.nutrition.phase; check athlete_params for next_phase_date.
leveragesInfra: send-weekly-checkin-reminder pattern (extend to physique). athlete_state.nutrition.phase + athlete_params (phase-gating). Existing PhysiqueTracker UI.

gap: Weekly ritual is weak — 'weekly check-in reminder' is vague; no clear 'log weigh-in + review numbers + approve plan' ceremony
whyItMatters: Elite coaches run Sunday reviews: weigh-in → look at trend + protein avg → adjust next week's plan. Nolan's app has scattered pieces (weigh-in modal, weekly plan card, meal plan reminder) but NO unified Sunday ritual. Users never close the loop = vague adherence = no trust that the engine is working.
proposedFill: New send-weekly-ritual-reminder function (fires Sunday 7pm). Push: "Weekly ritual time: weigh-in, review your numbers, approve next week's plan. 5 min to stay on track." Deep-link to new /WeeklyRitual page (minimal: big tappable weigh-in, 3-metric card [weight trend, protein avg, phase], approve-meal-plan CTA). On mobile, this becomes a sub-page of Today; on desktop it's a modal. Track ritual_completions table (user, date, weigh_in_logged, metrics_reviewed, plan_approved) to reward consistency.
leveragesInfra: send-weekly-meal-plan-reminder pattern + new ritual_completions table. Reuses WeighInModal, useDailyTargets hook, nutrition state. New lightweight page or modal.

gap: No missed-session re-engagement — if athlete skips a prescribed workout, app goes silent; zero nudge to log it or skip it formally
whyItMatters: Missed sessions are the #2 trust killer (after not logging). Athlete prescribes a strength day → athlete flakes → no feedback → athlete doubts the engine is adaptive. Coach-level products (Renaissance Periodization, MacroFactor) send same-day re-engagement: "Missed your session? Log it now or skip it (the engine will adjust)." Adherers WANT to stay accountable; the app should make it frictionless.
proposedFill: Track missed_sessions (user, prescribed_date, session_type, reminded_at, action='logged'|'skipped'|'still_open'). Extend send-reminder-push or new send-missed-session-nudge function. Fire at 22:00 if no workout_log exists for the prescribed date. Push: "You had a [Strength] session today. Log it now, or tap to skip (engine adjusts)" with two deep-links: /quick-workout?autoPopulate=true + /skip-session?date=TODAY. Skipping is a first-class action (updates daily_readiness + feeds notes_parser.py for adaptation).
leveragesInfra: training_prescription.mpc_action + workout_logs. New missed_sessions table. Existing send-reminder-push pattern + new skip-session endpoint. useTodayPrescription hook.

gap: No PR/milestone celebration or win notification — hitting a new deadlift max, a weight loss milestone, or a 7-day logging streak fires zero in-app celebration
whyItMatters: Dopamine hit from progress is THE retention hook. MacroFactor celebrates 'green week' (adherence win). Whoop celebrates 30-day streaks. Nolan's app is neutered here: log a new max → silent. Hit -10 lbs goal weight → silent. These are THE moments to cement identity ("I am someone who hits PRs").
proposedFill: New celebration_events table (user, event_type='pr_lift'|'weight_milestone'|'body_fat_drop'|'calorie_consistency'|'strength_milestone', value, prev_value, created_at). Trigger logic in: 1) workout logger on exercise save (compare load to exercise_reactions max for that lift), 2) athlete_state compute on weight trend alignment, 3) streak tracker on milestone hits (7/14/30/100 days). On app launch, show a dismissable banner: "🏆 New deadlift max! 455 → 465 lbs" with a share button (internal bragging) + permanent card in Insights. Push notification: same day, high-engagement copy.
leveragesInfra: athlete_state + workout_logs + exercise_reactions. New celebration_events + engagement_signals tables. Extends Insights page. Uses showLocalNotification for optional local toast.

gap: Notification fatigue tuning is absent — no frequency caps, timing preferences, or domain-based muting (e.g., 'don't nag me about nutrition on rest days')
whyItMatters: Push fatigue kills retention faster than any feature gap. User gets 3+ pushes/day = ignores by day 3 = unsubscribes. Elite apps (Whoop, MacroFactor) let users tune: 'brief only', 'only on train days', 'mute nutrition Sundays'. Today's app fires meal plan + brief + workout reminder + generic check-in = spammy.
proposedFill: New notification_preferences table (user, channel='daily_brief'|'meal_plan'|'workout_reminder'|'physique_checkin'|'weekly_ritual'|'streak_celebration', enabled, quiet_hours_start, quiet_hours_end, domain_filters=['training','nutrition','recovery'], max_per_day). UI: NotificationSettings.jsx expanded to show per-channel toggles + quiet hours + domain filters. Functions check prefs before sending. Default: all on, no quiet hours (opinionated but safe).
leveragesInfra: push_subscriptions table (add prefs_json or fork to notification_preferences). Extends NotificationSettings.jsx UI. All send-*-push functions query prefs before sending.

gap: No contextual re-engagement for lapsed logging — if athlete hasn't logged a daily readiness in 3+ days, app doesn't know and sends the same generic 'check-in' push to everyone
whyItMatters: Churn happens silently: user logs once, then life happens (busy week, travel, injury), logging drops off gradually. A smart system would detect 3-day gap and send HIGH-TOUCH re-engagement (not the same automation). Duolingo, Oura, MacroFactor all do this: "We haven't heard from you. Help us keep your data fresh — just 30 seconds."
proposedFill: New send-lapsed-logging-nudge function (daily cron, 19:00 UTC). Query: daily_readiness WHERE created_by=$1 AND checkin_date < (TODAY - 3 days) → send warm re-engagement push: "We miss your updates! Just 30 seconds: how's your energy today?" Include a 1-tap link to the MorningCheckin modal. Track lapsed_engagement_nudges (user, sent_at, opened, responded) to: 1) cap frequency (max 2/week), 2) surface in Insights if user is abandoning (build trust that the app is monitoring them).
leveragesInfra: daily_readiness + send-reminder-push pattern. New lapsed_engagement_nudges table. Existing MorningCheckin component.

gap: No weekly progress briefing or 'week in review' context before the plan push — athlete receives 'here's next week's plan' in a vacuum (no 'here's what you did last week' setup)
whyItMatters: Coach ritual: "Let's look back at what we did, celebrate the wins, then plan the week ahead." Nolan's send-weekly-meal-plan-reminder just says 'plan ready' with no context. Athlete has to manually scroll back to see if they crushed it or flopped. Missing this narrative = misses the feedback loop = no ownership.
proposedFill: Extend send-weekly-meal-plan-reminder to pre-send a send-weekly-progress-summary push (Sun 6pm, 1h before plan push). Content: pull from athlete_state (last 7d avg protein, trend, workout count from workout_logs) + celebration_events summary ("You hit a new max on 2 lifts this week!"). Push copy: "Here's your week in numbers: trained 4×, hit protein target 5 days, -0.3 lbs trend." Include a deep-link to new /WeeklyReview page (minimal: 4 metric cards [workouts, avg protein, weigh-ins, max PRs], no edits). Then 1h later, meal plan push lands with full context.
leveragesInfra: athlete_state + workout_logs + celebration_events. Extends send-weekly-meal-plan-reminder. New /WeeklyReview page (read-only summary).

gap: No early-phase onboarding boost — new users get the same push cadence as veterans; no extra touchpoints in week 1-2 to cement habit-forming behavior
whyItMatters: Habit formation research: first 14 days are critical. Slack, Discord, and Notion all turbocharge notifications + in-app prompts for new users ("Here's what to do next" every day for 2 weeks). Nolan's app treats day-1 athlete same as year-5. By week 3, casual users never logged enough to feel ownership = churn.
proposedFill: New onboarding_phase column (user_profiles.onboarding_phase = 'day_1_3'|'week_1_2'|'week_2_4'|'graduated'). Extend send-*-push functions with phase-gating. Day 1-3: send 3 pushes (morning brief + evening check-in + night recovery). Week 1-2: 2x daily (brief + reminder). Week 2+: standard cadence. Also: new send-onboarding-tip-of-day function (first 7 days only) + in-app banner: "Set your rest day + favorite exercises" (quick-setup). Track onboarding_completed as boolean once user logs 3 consecutive days.
leveragesInfra: user_profiles + all send-*-push functions. New send-onboarding-tip-of-day function. Existing in-app components.

gap: No first-run wearable pairing UX — new users never see setup for Garmin/Apple Health integration
whyItMatters: Without automated wearable sync, users manually log recovery metrics (HRV, sleep, steps, body battery), killing daily adherence. Garmin & Apple Health infrastructure exists (garmin-sync, health-webhook) but NO guided first-run setup prompts new users to connect. 80% of elite programs start data capture on day 1; OptiGains hides it.
proposedFill: Post-signup onboarding modal (3-step flow): (1) detect device type (iOS/Android); (2) prompt Garmin Connect OAuth2 OR Apple HealthKit permission; (3) trigger initial data sync (garmin-sync edge function). Surface status card on Dashboard showing "Wearable connected ✓" or "Connect your watch" CTA. Persist skip/snooze state to avoid nag fatigue.
leveragesInfra: Extends garmin-sync (already pulls HRV/sleep/RHR/body_battery/stress/VO2max), health-webhook (Apple Health payload ingestion), push subscription system (already deployed), recovery_metrics table (already stores biometrics). No new DB tables needed.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Data flow already proven in production. Modal is UI-only; wearable auth follows existing Supabase OAuth patterns (already used for email). Only new code: perm-gated onboarding flow + device detection.
competitorRef: MacroFactor & Whoop both front-load wearable setup as a core UX gate (can't use app without syncing). RP Strength and CalAI don't emphasize it (lower adherence in published data).

gap: Manual body-weight entry on every Profile save — no auto-sync from wearables despite Apple Health & Garmin both serving weight data
whyItMatters: Users manually type weight into Profile fields and save to log one entry. Garmin Watch & Apple Health both track daily weigh-ins; health-webhook already accepts weight payload. Missing friction point: the app requires friction where the wearable removes it. TDEE calculation (critical for nutrition modulation) needs accurate daily weight; manual entry = stale data = poor carb cycling.
proposedFill: Extend health-webhook to auto-sync weight from Apple Health daily. Add Garmin weight-sync endpoint (Garmin API has /wellness-service/wellness/bodyWeight). Add UI badge on Profile > Body weight field: "Last synced: 09:34 AM" with manual override. If synced weight differs >1 lb from last logged, prompt inline: "Auto-synced weight 175.2 lbs. Log as body-weight entry? [Yes / Skip]".
leveragesInfra: health-webhook already upserts body_weight_entries. Garmin-sync already handles OAuth2 token + API calls; add weight endpoint to its daily pull. usePushNotifications hook can trigger weigh-in prompt. body_weight_entries & user_profiles already have weight fields.
accuracyOrRisk: Low accuracy risk. Weight data from wearable carries timestamp ±0 (vs manual = hours later). Liability minimal: user always sees synced value before commit. Frame as "Assistant logged your weigh-in" not "Automatic" (gives user agency).
competitorRef: MacroFactor syncs weight from Apple Health automatically. Whoop surfaces weight trends from wearable. RP and CalAI both require manual entry (friction point).

gap: Recovery metrics page shows "Connect wearable" placeholder but never explains HOW or guides pairing flow
whyItMatters: RecoveryDetail.jsx line 335–336 shows "No biometric trends yet. Connect your wearable to populate HRV, step, and sleep charts." This is a demand without a fulfillment path. User taps it, nothing happens. They exit and never return. First-session drop-off is brutal; a $10k/mo coach would never leave users at this dead end.
proposedFill: RecoveryDetail empty state CTA button ("Connect Wearable") triggers the same onboarding modal. Or surface an in-card inline setup mini-flow: radio group ("Garmin" / "Apple Health") + "Next" CTA that launches device-specific auth. On completion, refetch recovery_metrics immediately so the chart populates live on the same screen.
leveragesInfra: No new infra. Reuse post-signup onboarding modal component OR create a reusable <WearableSetup> component. Recovery hook already invalidates on wearable data arrival.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. UX pattern is standard (unauth state → CTA → modal → auth → data fetch → UI updates). No new backend calls.
competitorRef: Whoop has a dedicated "Connect Devices" onboarding step that is visually unavoidable. MacroFactor's empty state flows directly to OAuth.

gap: No exercise history / preference auto-discovery during onboarding — Profile asks for available equipment but never probes favorite lifts or rep ranges
whyItMatters: OptiGains philosophy = high-intensity, sub-10-rep range, adaptive learning from session notes. But onboarding never asks "What do you usually lift?" or "Preferred rep ranges?" The adaptive engine trains on deviation/value; cold-start is weak without baseline preferences. Profile.jsx captures equipment + days/week but silently skips exercise priors. A $10k coach always asks movement baseline on day 1.
proposedFill: Extend Profile onboarding (or dedicated PostSignup.jsx page) with exercise history survey: (1) "Your strongest lifts?" [combobox: Squat / Bench / Deadlift / etc, with 1RM input]; (2) "Rep range you prefer?" [radio: 1-5 / 6-10 (default) / 11-15]; (3) "Exercises to avoid?" [multi-select from blocked list]. Store in user_profiles.{exercise_preferences, baseline_1rm, exercise_baseline_prefs} as jsonb. Pre-populate session_generator with these when available.
leveragesInfra: user_profiles already has exercise_preferences field (jsonb, currently unused in onboarding). session_generator already reads exercise_preferences.blocked. extend_prefs to include {preferred_rep_range, baseline_lifts, starting_1rm_estimate}. No new table.
accuracyOrRisk: Low accuracy risk — baseline is a prior, not gospel. User can revise in Profile anytime. Engine uses deviation (prescribed vs actual) to recalibrate; baseline just seeds the prior.
competitorRef: RP Strength mobile app has detailed exercise history intake ("best 5-rep squat", "weakest compound"). MacroFactor skips this (nutrition-only). Whoop does not ask (focus on recovery, not lift specifics).

gap: No scheduled or reminder-based health data re-sync — Garmin & Apple Health data captured once at signup, never re-synced unless user manually triggers cardio completion
whyItMatters: garmin-sync runs manually (via cron or edge-function trigger). health-webhook is webhook-only (passive, relies on external push). Neither is scheduled. User's watch accumulates 7 days of HRV/sleep/body_battery, but the app never fetches it. Recovery forecasts become stale; ACWR & readiness score drift. Missing data = missing $10k/mo value proposition ("coach sees everything").
proposedFill: Schedule daily Garmin recovery pull via Supabase cron (pg_cron extension already enabled). Create edge function health-sync-scheduler that fires daily 9 AM user-tz (using user_profiles.timezone). Trigger both on: (1) first app launch each day; (2) push notification ("Coach checking your recovery..."); (3) daily 9 AM cron (opt-in via NotificationSettings). Surface "Last synced 2 hours ago" timestamp in RecoveryDetail header so users trust freshness.
leveragesInfra: pg_cron already enabled (migrations enable it). garmin-sync function already deployed. health-webhook already handles payloads. send-daily-brief-push already sends scheduled pushes (reuse that pattern for sync reminder). Push subscription system already active.
