accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. Cron is idempotent; garmin-sync deduplicates. Health-webhook upserts with onConflict. Only new code: scheduler edge function + UX timestamp display. Privacy: user always controls sync frequency in NotificationSettings.
competitorRef: Whoop syncs continuously (wearable-native, real-time). MacroFactor syncs 2x daily by default. RP Strength relies on manual fetch (user friction). CalAI pulls weekly.

gap: No inline readiness/mood quick-capture at app launch or before workout — daily_readiness table exists but no mobile-optimized entry point
whyItMatters: daily_readiness.{energy, mood, soreness, sleep_score, stress_score} is the feedback loop training the adaptive engine. But there's NO first-screen prompt: "How are you today? [4/10 energy] [Good mood] [Sore: shoulders]". Users must navigate Profile > Body > scroll to find the form. Friction kills the feedback loop; engine runs blind. Elite coaches always capture readiness before workout (session performance correlates with pre-session state).
proposedFill: Create inline <DailyReadinessQuick> card (3 sliders: energy 1-10, mood, soreness 1-5) shown on Dashboard/Today above workout prescription. Persist state to daily_readiness on blur. Or surface as 20-second bottom sheet on app launch if not yet filled today. Icon button in header ("Pulse") to re-open anytime. Tie to push notification: "Coach wants to know: how are you feeling?" triggers the sheet.
leveragesInfra: daily_readiness table already exists (all fields present). useDailyReadiness hook can read/write. NotificationSettings already manages push opt-in. No new DB schema.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. UX is optional feedback, not required. Daily_readiness is already used by athlete_state recovery.score calculation (see RecoveryDetail line 118–120). More data = better signal, but not critical if user skips.
competitorRef: Whoop leads with readiness score + "How are you feeling?" prompt. MacroFactor doesn't capture mood (nutrition-only). RP Strength has optional readiness form. Whoop's mobile UX is gold standard here.

gap: No nutritional baseline capture during onboarding — users never specify current diet type, restrictions, or foods they track
whyItMatters: Nutrition goals are calculated in Profile from TDEE + macro goals, but there's no intake of current diet baseline (vegan, paleo, low-carb, etc). usda-proxy edge function can search foods, but cold-start is weeks of manual logging. A $10k coach would ask "What do you usually eat?" on day 1 to seed meal_templates & custom_foods. Missing this kills nutrition adherence on week 1.
proposedFill: Post-signup onboarding (or Profile > Fuel tab): (1) "Diet type?" [radio: Omnivore / Vegan / Keto / Low-Carb / etc]; (2) "Restrictions?" [multi-select: Dairy-free / Gluten-free / Nut allergy / etc]; (3) "Your go-to meals?" [free text × 3 meal examples]. Optionally seed meal_templates from template library matching user's diet type. Store restrictions in user_profiles.dietary_restrictions jsonb.
leveragesInfra: user_profiles can add dietary_restrictions field (jsonb). meal_templates already exist. Could seed templates from a hardcoded library (seeds.ts) or Supabase public table. No breaking changes.
accuracyOrRisk: Low accuracy risk — restrictions are data quality hints, not constraints. User can deviate anytime. But catching allergies/intolerances early is a small safety guard.
competitorRef: MacroFactor asks diet type on signup. Whoop doesn't (not nutrition-focused). RP Strength has a food preferences section (optional). CalAI has no dietary intake (template-based only).

gap: No physique baseline capture — users can upload photos day 1 but app never asks for starting measurements or asks to establish pose baseline
whyItMatters: PhysiqueTracker requires photo comparison (side-by-side delta). But cold-start means a new user uploads one photo, has no comparison, sees no trend. The compare feature lives dormant for weeks. Pose instructions are clear, but app never prompts "Let's establish your baseline: take 6 poses front/back/side, flexed/relaxed." A smart app would gamify: "Baseline complete ✓ → unlock trend tracking!".
proposedFill: Post-signup onboarding (or lazy-loaded on first /physique visit): guided 6-shot session (FRONT_RELAXED → FRONT_FLEX → SIDE → ABS_THIGHS → BACK_RELAX → BACK_FLEX). Each step shows pose cue + photo preview. Save all 6 as day-1 batch entry. Then show "Baseline established! Come back in 2 weeks for your first comparison." This removes friction to day-1 compliance.
leveragesInfra: PhysiqueTracker + analyze-physique function already handle multi-pose capture. physique_entries already support pose field. No schema change needed. Just UX orchestration.
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk. All features already exist; this is a guided UX wrapper. Pose cues already in the code.
competitorRef: Whoop doesn't track physique. MacroFactor doesn't. RP Strength has a "baseline photos" section but no guided intake. This is a gap for all competitors; OptiGains could own it.

gap: No coaching intake form — Profile asks body stats & goals, but never captures training experience level, injury history, or prior program context
whyItMatters: The adaptive engine (Science.md) is built on *learned* priors (MEV/MAV/MRV per muscle). But cold-start has no baseline. A new user says "I'm 175 lbs, want to get lean" but the system doesn't know if they're a novice squatting 185 lbs or an intermediate at 405. Session_generator prescribes volume blindly; the engine learns from 2 weeks of data. But a real coach would say "OK, walk me through your training history." This input seeds better initial prescriptions.
proposedFill: Dedicated Coach Intake form (PostSignup.jsx or Profile > Identity): (1) "Training age?" [radio: <1 yr / 1-3 yr / 3-5 yr / 5+ yr]; (2) "Prior programs?" [text: "5/3/1", "PPL", "Jacked & Tan", etc]; (3) "Injury/limitation history?" [textarea + list of commonly-avoided exercises]; (4) "Goals 12-week horizon?" [multi-select: Strength / Hypertrophy / Endurance / Leanness / Sport-perf]. Store as user_profiles.training_history, user_profiles.prior_programs, user_profiles.injury_notes, user_profiles.coach_intake_date (jsonb).
leveragesInfra: user_profiles already has injuries_limitations field (barely used). Extend to structured intake. athlete_goals table exists (unused). Could log intake as athlete_goals entries for the engine to read.
accuracyOrRisk: Low accuracy risk. Intake is self-reported; user can always revise. But it seeds better adaptive priors, reducing cold-start error.
competitorRef: RP Strength has detailed intake (lifting history, mobility, injury detail). MacroFactor doesn't. Whoop has minimal intake. CalAI has none.

gap: No photo-based food logging. FoodTracker.jsx is USDA-search + barcode only; there is zero AI capture path despite a working Groq-vision pipeline (analyze-physique: signed-URL -> vision model -> strict-JSON -> DB insert).
whyItMatters: Manual macro entry is the #1 adherence killer in nutrition apps. Cal AI's entire wedge is 'snap a photo, get macros in 3 seconds.' For a $10k coach the bottleneck isn't the algorithm (OptiGains' adaptive TDEE already rivals MacroFactor) — it's whether the user actually logs every day. Friction here directly degrades the trend-weight + intake signal the whole TDEE engine depends on, so the gap compounds: bad logging -> bad expenditure estimate -> wrong targets.
proposedFill: New analyze-meal edge function cloned from analyze-physique: upload meal photo to a private bucket, signed URL to the Groq vision model with a strict-JSON prompt ({items:[{name,grams,calories,protein,carbs,fats}], confidence}), pre-fill the existing food-entry form (user confirms/edits before save). Tag entries source='photo' + confidence so the engine can down-weight low-confidence days in the intake-bias learner.
leveragesInfra: analyze-physique vision pipeline (signed URL + vision + extractJSON pattern is line-for-line reusable), physique private-bucket pattern, existing food_entries schema + FoodTracker edit form, usda-proxy for cross-checking matched items.
competitorRef: Cal AI (photo->macros is their whole product)
accuracyOrRisk: Photo macros are approximate — must show editable estimate + confidence, never silent-save. Same honesty framing analyze-physique already uses ('value is trend, not a precise number').

gap: No natural-language food logging. There is no 'describe what you ate' text path — every entry requires structured search + serving math.
whyItMatters: Photo logging fails for restaurant meals, mixed dishes, and 'I had a protein shake and 2 eggs.' MacroFactor and Cal AI both ship text/voice quick-log because typed natural language is faster than search-and-scale for compound meals. Lower friction = more complete logs = a cleaner intake series for the adaptive TDEE engine.
proposedFill: Extend the same analyze-meal function with a text mode: free-text -> Groq -> itemized macro JSON -> pre-filled confirmable rows. Wire it to the existing search sheet as a second input mode (a 'describe it' toggle next to the USDA search box). Reuse recent-foods + custom_foods as grounding context in the prompt to match the user's known items.
leveragesInfra: generate-daily-brief Groq text-call pattern, FoodTracker search sheet + recent/custom-food surfacing, food_entries schema.
competitorRef: MacroFactor (text quick-log), Cal AI (describe-a-meal)
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — user confirms before write; grounding on custom_foods improves match accuracy and avoids hallucinated brands.

gap: Adaptive-TDEE math is best-in-class but barely surfaced. The Forbes-composition expenditure estimate, learned intake bias, and weekly trend exist in tdee.py and Progress.jsx shows a single expenditure number, but there's no MacroFactor-style expenditure-vs-intake trend chart or weekly program-update narrative ('your expenditure rose 90 kcal, targets adjusted').
whyItMatters: MacroFactor's signature trust-builder is the weekly check-in that VISIBLY recalculates and explains. OptiGains computes a more sophisticated estimate than MacroFactor but hides the reasoning, so the user can't see the engine working — which is exactly the deep-trust dimension a $10k coach sells. Trust drives adherence to the (sometimes uncomfortable) target changes.
proposedFill: An expenditure dashboard card: trend line of estimated TDEE over time + logged intake overlay + trend-weight, plus a weekly 'what changed and why' line generated from the engine deltas (deficit_ratio, intake_bias, weeks_in_phase). Surface the diet-break / reverse-diet triggers (already computed in nutrition_modulator + phase_recommender) as proactive cards instead of leaving them buried in athlete_state.
leveragesInfra: tdee.py outputs already in athlete_state.nutrition, nutrition_modulator.recommend_deficit rationale strings, phase_recommender reverse_diet flag, generate-daily-brief for the weekly narrative, existing Progress.jsx expenditure read.
competitorRef: MacroFactor (expenditure dashboard + weekly adjustment explainer)
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — surfaces math that already runs. Honesty: label as estimate with the same trend-not-absolute framing.

gap: No exercise technique/cue surfacing or auto-regulated per-set feedback during logging. exerciseLibrary.js HAS step-by-step instructions but they are never shown in the session view; the notes_parser diagnoses sticking points server-side but the lifter gets no in-session cue.
whyItMatters: RP Hypertrophy's value is the coach in your ear: 'this set should be RIR 2 — if the last rep wasn't a grind, add load.' OptiGains already computes the autoregulation server-side (e1RM slope -> INCREASE_LOAD/HOLD, sticking-point -> assistance) but the lifter executing the set sees none of it, so the intelligence doesn't change behavior at the moment it matters. Better in-set guidance = better load selection = better progression signal back to the engine.
proposedFill: In ExerciseCard, render a one-line autoregulation cue derived from the engine's existing per-exercise command + RIR target (e.g. 'Last 3 weeks trending up — go +2.5 lb' or 'Stall flagged: focus lockout, technique cue available'). Add a tap-to-expand technique/cue panel from exerciseLibrary instructions. Show the prior-session e1RM delta inline.
leveragesInfra: strength_progression command + athlete_state.strength (already computed), notes_parser sticking-point output, exerciseLibrary.js instructions (already loaded, just unsurfaced), ExerciseCard RIR/last-time UI.
competitorRef: RP Hypertrophy (per-set RIR-driven load guidance + cues)
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk — advisory only, matches fatigueManagement's 'never block' convention.

gap: No PR detection / personal-records logbook. WorkoutDetail computes e1RM but never flags a PR, and there's no per-exercise history/logbook view the way Hevy/Strong surface 'best set, best e1RM, all-time history.'
whyItMatters: PRs are the dopamine loop that keeps lifters logging — Hevy/Strong's stickiest feature. OptiGains has all the data (workout_logs + e1RM math) but turns none of it into a moment. Celebrating a PR mid-session reinforces the high-intensity/low-volume identity the app is built around, and the per-exercise logbook is what makes a lifter trust they're actually progressing.
proposedFill: PR toast on set save when load, reps-at-load, or e1RM beats the exercise's history (data already fetched in WorkoutDetail for autofill). A per-exercise logbook view (history list + e1RM sparkline) reachable from ExerciseCard, reusing the existing e1RM projection helper.
leveragesInfra: WorkoutDetail already fetches full per-exercise workout_logs history for autofill, existing Epley e1RM helper, usePushNotifications local-notification (already used for rest timer) for the toast.
competitorRef: Hevy / Strong (PR badges + per-exercise logbook)
accuracyOrRisk: Low risk.

gap: No training-load / strain target. recoveryUtils computes ACWR + a readiness-based training-capacity (hours), but there's no Whoop-style daily strain target that says 'today's recovery supports THIS much load' tied to the actual session, and no closed loop showing achieved-vs-recommended load.
whyItMatters: Whoop's signature is recovery -> recommended strain -> did-you-hit-it. OptiGains gates volume/RIR on HRV in the engine (the philosophy-correct downregulation: cut volume at held load, never drop the bar), but the user never sees a concrete 'recovery budget' number for today or whether they spent it. Surfacing the recovery_budget band makes the no-programmed-deloads philosophy legible and trustworthy instead of invisible.
proposedFill: A daily recovery-budget card: today's readiness -> a recommended session-load band (sets/hard-set count, NOT a load cut), then after the session show achieved load vs band. Drives the existing 'cut volume/RIR at held load' rule into a visible target the user can hit, with a gentle nudge when ACWR > 1.3.
leveragesInfra: recoveryUtils calculateTrainingCapacity + calculateACWR, recovery_metrics/daily_readiness, athlete_state.fatigue, trainingLoad.js, RecoveryDetail page.

gap: Offline logging robustness is unproven for the gym use-case. The service worker is cache-first for assets, but food/workout writes go straight through React Query/Supabase with no offline queue, and gyms routinely have dead cell/wifi.
whyItMatters: Strong/Hevy are trusted because a set logged in a basement gym never disappears. If a write fails on a flaky connection mid-session, the lifter loses sets and stops trusting the logger — and missing sets corrupt the deviation-tracker and volume signals the engine learns from. Reliability is table-stakes for the logging UX these apps win on.
proposedFill: Offline write queue for workout-set and food saves: optimistic local persist (IndexedDB) + background-sync flush when connection returns, with a subtle 'pending sync' indicator. Scope to the two hot write paths (useWorkoutSession set saves, food_entries insert) rather than a full offline rewrite.
leveragesInfra: existing service worker registration in main.jsx, React Query mutation layer in useWorkoutSession + FoodTracker, Supabase client.
